summary: Claude was clearly more accurate on this image. It swept all four visible silhouette corners (both top and both base) placing them on the true casting/slab vertices, whereas codex committed a systematic corner error: its back (image-left) corners float in empty black background ~140-195px outside the machine, and both its base corners sit ~210px too high at the body/slab junction instead of the slab bottom. Claude also correctly marked the visible pinion sprocket and crank-axle sprocket, which codex wrongly called occluded/omitted. Codex's only edge was in the heavily-occluded base gear window, where its cylinder-gear points sat on actual brass cylinder forms while claude's cyl1 landed on a vertical comb screw — but that region is low-confidence for both.
